articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Industrial LANs for Management, Design and Manufacture' (Digest No.190)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Industrial LANs for Management, Design and Manufacture
IEE Colloquium on Industrial LANs for Management, Design and Manufacture
abstract: Field Bus is the familiar name for a communications standard which is an ongoing initiative assigned to TC65/SC65c/WG6 of the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC). Field Bus is a communication system which is expressly designed for process control and especially concerning the 'real time' constraints of physically or chemically dynamic systems. A summary of the requirement, status and commercial consequences of Field Bus is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Industrial LANs for Management, Design and Manufacture
abstract: In 1986 NMUK completed the first phase of construction of its new car manufacturing plant in Sunderland, which had the capability of producing 24000 units per year. Since then there have been two further expansions increasing the manufacturing capacity to 270000 units per year. Such rapid expansion creates many problems. One of the problems was deciding how best to monitor and control the huge individual production shops and how to link them together to make it one effective production facility. One of the solutions to this problem has been local area networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Installation of LANs-the pitfalls and hardware requirements
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Industrial LANs for Management, Design and Manufacture
abstract: The author discusses factors that need to be considered in the design, planning and implementation of a new LAN or the extension of an existing LAN. Emphasis is placed on the need to conform to the relevant standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of an open systems network
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Industrial LANs for Management, Design and Manufacture
abstract: NEI Parsons is a Pounds 100 million/annum turnover business, employing 2000 people across a site of approximately 4000 acres. The company's main business is the design, manufacture, site installation and after-sales servicing of steam turbine plant, combined gas/steam cycle plant and power generators for the world market. The mainframe facility has been closed down and a three year facility management contract taken out to support those mainframe operations from a remote site. Mainframe applications are to be migrated onto a distributed network of workstations, servers and PCs. The first stage of this exercise is the creation of a company-wide local area network. The wiring strategy and the protocol strategy are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Industrial LANs for Management, Design and Manufacture
abstract: The author presents a very short overview of the basic characteristics of local area networks, including the three main LANs (Ethernet, token ring and FDDI) followed by a description of the issues concerning industrial LANs in particular. Future technologies are very briefly discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: NetWare in practice: the glue for heterogeneous systems development
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Industrial LANs for Management, Design and Manufacture
abstract: There are a large number of connectivity products available for stand along PCs of for the NetWare Network environment. NetWare's role is one of a platform upon which these implementation strategies may be built. With NetWare at the centre acting as the glue to which many different systems may be connected, complex architectures may be implemented with few or no visible seams to complicate the user's life. Resources and data may be shared across the enterprise and the right tools can be selected for each individual task-making it possible to create a truly supportive IT environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Industrial LANs for Management, Design and Manufacture
abstract: The author gives an insight into BT's experience in the interconnection of LANs used to support its own internal commercial computing applications. He describes the current drivers for change and explains the current strategic developments. The paper focuses on the wide area networking issues created by the need to provide a large number of remote LANs with access to nationwide computing resources.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
